direction: Treat a correction as a pointer to the last thing said, fix only that, confirm it, and have a second way out when speech keeps failing.
dont_over_correct: Do not read back every detail of every turn, which slows calls. Do not ask the caller to repeat when you already have a confident, corrected value. Do not treat every "no" as a correction ("No, that's all" ends the call).
prompt: Treat a correction as a pointer to the last thing said, change only that detail, and read the new value back.
design: Repair the slot, not the whole turn.
Ask a targeted question when unsure.
Read the new value back and wait for a yes.
Honor "say that again" and "stop" at once.
Hand off after two failed repairs
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: turn.text, repair.count, repair.method, state.slot_values, reply.text?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the system prompt?

evals.behaviour: Day correction: A correction changes only the named detail
evals.pass_if: One slot changes; the rest stay
evals.fail_if: The whole state resets or the old value stays

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: "No, that's all.": A correction changes only the named detail
evals.pass_if: One slot changes; the rest stay
evals.fail_if: The whole state resets or the old value stays

guardrail.condition: the caller corrects a detail or asks for a repeat, and again after each failed repair, and the reply breaks the rule: treat a correction as a pointer to the last thing said, change only that detail, and read the new value back.
